knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Standing the board on its edge lets both faces drain and dry. Water that sits in the grooves supports residue and odour.
Sanitiser must come from an approved product at the label dilution. Topping up with another product, or using a stronger mix, is not an acceptable substitute.
A board whose crack holds residue that the sequence cannot clear is taken out of use and reported for replacement, and it is not stored with boards in service.

practicalCriteria: Puts on the PPE that the approved label lists before opening the sanitiser, observed by the assessor.
Runs a supplied board through scrape, wash, rinse, sanitise at the label dilution and contact time, rinse, and dry on edge, in that order, observed by the assessor.
Declines to mix products when the sanitiser runs out, and makes up a labelled fresh batch from the approved product instead, observed by the assessor.
Identifies a supplied board with a crack, takes it out of use, and completes a written report, observed by the assessor.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation sheet for the board sequence
Labelled sanitiser batch record for the practical run
Report of the board taken out of use
stopWorkCriteria: The sanitiser container is unlabelled, or its product is not on the approved list
A worker is about to mix the sanitiser with another product or top it up
A worker has a skin reaction, eye contact or breathing symptoms from a product: stop, follow the first aid steps on the label, and report it
A board is about to be sanitised at a strength above the label dilution
